answer: A costly reputation signal can separate real agents from fake ones: each agent must stake tokens and build a verifiable history of useful work before it can earn, so creating thousands of identities becomes expensive rather than free. The fable of the sparrow that pretended to be a flock by copying its own shadow is a warning — duplicates look alike under inspection, and a system that checks work history, stake, and peer attestations together makes mass forgery unprofitable, because every fake identity must pay the same price as a real one.
